LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset. … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20 Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. away.headline: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out
away.blurb: Rams Injury Report, Week 9 at Commanders: Myles Garrett expected to play; Trent McDuffie, Colby Parkinson, and Kam Curl questionable; Terrance Ferguson ruled out Skip to main content Primary nav TEAM "We're still working through those types of things," McVay said Friday morning prior to practice, when asked what kind of ramp-up he expects in terms of how much Garrett is able to play on Sunday. "He's really done a great job in practice. He'll be a DNP today, but it's more of just being smart with him. Nothing to do with anything other than he has progressed really well, made a tremendous impact in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, feels really comfortable with the game plan, and it's been great having him out there, as well as (tight end) Terrance (Ferguson)." While Ferguson (ankle) also returned to practice this week, and was expected to play Sunday according to McVay, he ended up being ruled out after the Rams sent out an updated injury report. Initially listed on this week's report with an ankle injury, Ferguson picked up a hamstring injury in Friday's practice based on the injury updated report. Meanwhile, Trent McDuffie (back) and tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) are listed as questionable for Sunday's game, as well as inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and safety Kam Curl (foot). Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) is listed as doubtful, which would set up Jake McQuaide to be up from the practice squad again. McVay also said cornerback Jaylen Watson is listed as out, but will be placed on IR. Otherwise, all other Rams players listed on the injury report do not have a game status designation. For the Commanders, wide receivers Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) have been ruled out, while defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) is listed as questionable. away.blurb: Commanders-Giants Final Injury Report: Lucas Patrick Out, Treylon Burks Expected Back Despite Missed Practice Skip to main content SI.COM Lucas Patrick is out Thursday night against the New York Giants. The Commanders’ final injury report also ruled out tight end Colson Yankoff, leaving Washington to start Nick Allegretti at center in place of Patrick. Patrick entered concussion protocol during Sunday’s loss to the Rams, and rookie Matt Gulbin finished that game at center. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Tuesday that Allegretti will start against New York. Gulbin got the call Sunday because he had been taking the center reps while Allegretti worked at guard, a decision I wrote more about earlier this week . According to Washington's official website, the Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL. Allegretti will have to help set the protection against that defense with Jayden Daniels behind him. Treylon Burks missed Wednesday’s practice with the foot injury that kept him out against the Rams, but he has no game designation. Quinn said the day off was planned after Burks got work Tuesday and that the receiver was expected to be ready Thursday. Washington did not practice Monday and held a walkthrough Tuesday, so those first two participation reports were estimates. Burks’ place on the active list will be confirmed with Thursday’s inactives. Yankoff did not practice during the short week because of a knee injury. His absence reaches beyond the tight end rotation: Washington credited him with 185 special teams snaps this season. John Bates (shoulder) was full all three days, and Chig Okonkwo (hip) was full Tuesday and Wednesday. Neither has a game designation. home.headline: Giants' Malik Nabers Says 'I Kind of Lost Myself' During Recovery from Major Knee Injury
home.blurb: Raanan pointed out that Nabers hadn't suffered a serious injury to that point in his football career. Experiencing this for the first time and not knowing when he'd be back weighed on him. Bleacher Report • 2h Jim Harbaugh Calls Out Broncos 😒 Bleacher Report • 2h Caleb Wilson Out 4-6 Weeks Bleacher Report • 6h Steph Out 2+ Weeks with Oblique Tear New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers discussed in candid detail his lengthy recovery from a torn ACL in 2025. The third-year wideout told ESPN's Jordan Raanan he "kind of lost myself in the process." "Everybody didn't know what my mindset was," Nabers said. "Just at a loss for words. Didn't really have a lot of words to say. Didn't really have, I don't know, I kind of was empty. Just didn't know what the future holds, how I was going to respond, just with everything that was going on. Everybody just didn't know." The 2024 Pro Bowler added that he struggled to articulate his internal thoughts. "Just didn't know how to communicate how I was feeling and how things were going because every day it was something new," he said. "... So I just didn't know, I just didn't really see a process. I didn't really see progress from week to week." The 2026 season got off to an uneven start for Nabers. After an encouraging showing in a Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys, he combined to have six receptions for 27 yards in the Giants' next two games. Now, the 23-year-old is hitting his stride again. From Week 4 on, he has averaged 110.4 receiving yards per game with two touchdowns. ▶️Full Saints-Giants Recap 05:39 The Giants have a lot of reasons to be happy as they sit first in the NFC East at 5-2-1. The Patriots, which are off to a 5-4 start, are coming off a 45-27 defeat at the hands of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Meanwhile, the Lions, which are sitting at 6-2, defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, in their Week 9 tilt . New England – led by Mike Vrabel on the sidelines – has lost two of its last three games, including to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Additionally, it sits basically in the middle of the pack in both points scored (23.4/game) and points allowed (23.0/g). Yet, the Patriots still possess a myriad of talent on both sides of the ball. On offense, they're led under center by third-year passer Drake Maye, who has thrown for 18 touchdowns, 2,282 yards and a league-high 11 interceptions through nine games. He's coming off a three-interception performance against the Packers in which he completed a season-low 55.3 percent of his passes. Maye's top target this year has been veteran tight end Hunter Henry, who has amassed 32 catches, 361 yards and two touchdowns through the season's first nine games. And on the ground, the Patriots are spearheaded by sixth-year back Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson, a fourth-round pick of New England, has accumulated 399 yards and two touchdowns, and is presently averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Then, on the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots have received strong performances this season from the likes of EDGE defenders Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, cornerback Carlton Davis III and linebacker Christian Elliss. Ponder, a second-year pro , has already recorded 7.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and 13 QB hits, and has returned a fumble for a touchdown. And for his efforts, he's earned a 75.0 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the 23rd-best overall grade among 110 qualified players at the position. The Patriots will not, however, have the services of Davis (knee) for this Week 10 international affair. Plus, they will also be down starting left guard Ben Brown (knee), and are expected to be without Stevenson (knee). Stevenson, the team's No. 1 back, suffered a plantaris tendon tear last week against the Packers. Those are three significant losses for Vrabel's squad going into its matchup with Detroit. As for the Lions, they will also be down multiple starters in Week 10: linebacker Jack Campbell (neck), center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip). Plus, safety Kerby Joseph, who has yet to play a single game in 2026, will not be making his season debut in Germany. While both teams are rather significantly banged up, I still believe this matchup favors Detroit. At this present juncture, I believe the Lions have a 59 percent chance to secure their fifth straight victory. Lions (6-2) have won four consecutive games. Pats are 8-5 all-time against Lions. Kickoff is set for 9:30 a.m. ET Sunday at Allianz Arena in Munich. After a brutal 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers at home, the New England Patriots are off to Germany to take on another tough NFC North opponent in Week 10. The Patriots and Lions will face off Sunday at Allianz Arena in Munich. New England enters with a 5-4 record, while Detroit is 6-2 and riding a four-game win streak. Pats quarterback Drake Maye hopes to bounce back after throwing three interceptions in the loss to Green Bay. The 2025 NFL MVP runner-up is tied for the NFL lead with 11 INTs. Lions QB Jared Goff has thrown only two interceptions all season, but both INTs came in his last two games. He led Detroit to a 19-9 win over Miami last week despite throwing for only 170 yards with zero touchdowns. Will Maye and the Patriots rebound from last Sunday's woeful performance, or will they remain winless against NFC opponents this season? Here's our Week 10 preview and prediction: Recent head-to-head matchups The Patriots are 8-5 all-time against the Lions. They've won five of their last six meetings with Detroit, though they had Tom Brady at quarterback for all but one of those games. On Sunday, Maye will face the Lions for the first time in his young NFL career. Week 5, 2022 at New England: 29-0 Patriots Week 3, 2018 at Detroit: 26-10 Lions Week 12, 2014 at New England: 34-9 Patriots Turnover differential Neither the Patriots nor the Lions excel at forcing turnovers. Both rank near the bottom of the league with only eight takeaways apiece. Still, Detroit has a positive turnover differential (+3) because of its ability to limit giveaways. Quarterback Jared Goff has thrown only two interceptions this season, and the Lions have turned it over only five times total. That's where Detroit has a significant advantage over New England. The Pats are tied with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for the most giveaways (19) this season. Maye is tied with Chargers QB Justin Herbert for the league lead in interceptions (11). Secondary struggles The Patriots have one of the NFL's best cornerbacks in Christian Gonzalez. In the offseason, they added last year's INT leader in veteran safety Kevin Byard. Veteran CB Carlton Davis, speedy CB Marcus Jones, and promising young safety Craig Woodson added to what was expected to be one of the NFL's best secondaries in 2026. The group hasn't lived up to those lofty expectations through the first nine weeks. New England is in the middle of the pack (14th) with 328.6 passing yards allowed per game. Of course, that number was inflated after Gonzalez and Co.'s woeful performance last week vs. the Packers, during which they allowed wideouts Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to combine for 335 yards and two touchdowns. It won't get any easier for the Pats secondary this Sunday against the Lions' top two wideouts, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. The good news for New England? The Lions have allowed the seventh-most passing yards per game (355). However, their secondary has greatly improved as of late, allowing only 226 passing yards per game while notching at least one interception in each of their last four games. Patriots' key to victory Win the turnover battle How could this not be the key to a Patriots victory after reading those turnover differential stats? Maye's three interceptions in last week's loss to Green Bay were a killer, but they weren't totally unexpected as the Packers rank near the top of the league in takeaways. A repeat performance against a Lions team that hardly turns the ball over would be disastrous. Lions' key to victory Keep the pressure on Drake Maye Detroit's defense ranks seventh in the NFL in pressure rate (25.7 percent) and second in sacks (27). New England's offensive line will be tasked with containing the fearsome trio of Aidan Hutchinson (5 sacks, 6 tackles for loss), Alim McNeill (5.5 sacks, 6.5 TFL), and DJ Wonnum (5 sacks, 5 TFL). The Lions' pass rushers should be licking their chops with a chance to disrupt the turnover-prone Maye. The Patriots might have to abandon the run without their top two running backs, Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness), so it could be a long day for the Pats' offense if Maye is consistently under pressure. If the Patriots' offense were at full strength, we may have given them the slight edge in this matchup. But as of Thursday, it looks like they could be without A.J. Brown (ankle and knee), Romeo Doubs (injured reserve, shoulder), Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), and TreVeyon Henderson (illness). That'll be difficult to overcome, even against this beatable Detroit defense. Turnovers will be the difference in this one. New England simply doesn't do a good enough job of protecting the football, and Detroit is among the league's best in that department. The Lions are currently 2.5-point favorites for the Week 10 showdown in Germany, and we see them winning fairly convincingly. Score : 30-20 Lions

The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It's been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it'll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots' 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers' worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: "Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven't turned the ball over, they haven't exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it's just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven't quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error." The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

away.blurb: Rhamondre Stevenson "wants to be out there" for Patriots "I think that just speaks to, first off, the media not really knowing 100 percent what they’re talking about a lot of the time," Maye said, as shared by Mark Daniels of MassLive. "First off, a guy that wants to be out there. Wants to be back for his team. We’re in the midst of trying to make a run here and win a big one before the bye. So, this is a time for a lot of the players on this team to try and get out there, play for their teammates. He’s a great player, and he can help us out." Fellow Patriots ball-carrier TreVeyon Henderson is said to be out indefinitely after he recently "experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms." As for Stevenson, he leads the Patriots with 102 carries and 399 rushing yards this season. Over nine games, he rushed for two touchdowns. Those comments would lead one to believe that Stevenson could at least be a game-time decision regarding the Week 10 matchup. A recent report suggested that the 5-4 New England Patriots would be without lead running back Rhamondre Stevenson for at least the club's game against the 6-2 Detroit Lions in Munich , Germany. If Stevenson can't go against Detroit, third-choice option and second-year undrafted player Corey Kiner would be on track to serve as New England's RB1. "I know some people that probably, like, 'Man, I ain't even finna try.' But his situation, man, I be talking to him be like, 'I finna try. I finna do what I can do,'" Douglas said about Stevenson. Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a plantaris tendon issue in the back of his knee. He won't need surgery, according to Rapoport. The 28-year-old exited New England's Week 9 loss to the Green Bay Packers early. He has 102 carries for 399 yards and two touchdowns this season. New England's running back injuries leave Corey Kiner and Lan Larison as the team's top options on the depth chart. The Patriots are second in the AFC East with a 5-4 record. away.headline: Lions rule out 3 players for game vs. Patriots in Germany
away.blurb: News Sports Autos Business Michigan Life + Home Entertainment Opinion Obituaries LIONS Lions rule out 3 players for game vs. Patriots in Germany Richard Silva The Detroit News Nov. 12, 2026, 5:10 p.m. ET Hear this story View Comments MUNICH, Germany — Three members of the Detroit Lions have already been ruled out for the team's game against the New England Patriots in Munich on Sunday, Nov. 15, including center Cade Mays (ankle), cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) and safety Kerby Joseph (knee). None of those designations should come as a surprise, as Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Nov. 10 he didn't see Joseph making his season debut at Allianz Arena. One day later, Campbell said Mays and Reed only had a "way, way, way outside shot" to be available. Joseph returned to practice Oct. 28 and has been working his way back. The good news is Joseph was listed as a full participant at practice Thursday; he had yet to be a full participant at any practice this season. Mays and Reed were each injured in Detroit's 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1 . Both players were held out of a matchup against the Miami Dolphins on Nov. 8. Quarterback Jared Goff (chest) and safety Brian Branch (hip) were listed as limited participants at practice Wednesday but were upgraded to full participants Thursday. Running back Sione Vaki (ankle) missed practice Wednesday and Thursday, and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited in each session. The Lions could still rule out other players ahead of their game against the Patriots, but they had to officially sideline Mays, Reed and Joseph because none of those three are traveling with the team to Germany. Defensive end D.J. Wonnum (concussion) and running back Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring) were full participants Wednesday and Thursday.

away.headline: Patriots final Week 9 injury report: Good news, bad news
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Star wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have already been ruled out for the game. The Patriots might also be missing tight end Hunter Henry, who is still battling the foot injury he suffered in last week's win over the Miami Dolphins. Veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins and interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten both returned from injured reserve this week to practice. They are officially listed as questionable to play against the Packers. The New England Patriots will once again be shorthanded on the offensive side of the ball when hosting the Green Bay Packers for a visit on Sunday. But it isn't all bad news for the Patriots. Hollins has been one of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's most reliable downfield targets, and Van Roten was the top replacement at right guard behind Mike Onwenu. Those returns would be a huge lift to a Patriots offense that needs all of the help it can get. home.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
home.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." After missing back-to-back weeks due to a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September, the former All-Pro returned as a limited participant to begin Detroit Lions prep. But running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed among the sidelined in Foxborough and have officially been ruled out for the matchup in Munich. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) An illness that kept Henderson hospitalized for multiple days will now keep the running back out for a third straight game. The Patriots will be without another Brown on offense after the team’s starting left guard exited last Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. And in the secondary, a knee injury will also keep Davis from taking the field in Munich after he’d worked back from a neck injury throughout October. That leaves four non-participants from Wednesday potentially in play for the NFL international series. After Van Roten headed back to practice last week, Gilliam did so to start work on the Lions. The fullback spent the past five games on injured reserve. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Both the Chiefs (6-2) and the Falcons (3-6) meet Sunday afternoon in Atlanta. They are each within one half-game of first place in their respective divisions. The Broncos lead Kansas City in the AFC West while the Falcons are looking up at the Panthers and the Saints in the NFC South. This despite Atlanta having lost two in a row and the Chiefs two of their last three. Kansas City is coming off a convincing 35-12 win over the New York Jets, a game that turned after the Chiefs trailed 12-7 in the second quarter. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both scoring passes going to Kenneth Walker III , who was the offensive centerpiece with 102 rushing yards, 143 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Travis Kelce added 72 receiving yards and even scored on a one-yard run. The defense took over after halftime, holding New York scoreless in the final thirty minutes as the Chiefs pulled away with 21 unanswered second-half points. Kansas City also went 4-for-4 in the red zone, an encouraging development after back-to-back losses to Seattle and Denver. Mahomes did briefly leave the field after hurting his arm/elbow on a strip-sack but returned and finished the game. As a result, the injury report is worth following as gametime approaches. Atlanta, meanwhile, returns home after a disappointing 34-17 loss to Cincinnati in Madrid, its second straight defeat following a 16-0 shutout loss at Tampa Bay. The Falcons opened strongly against the Bengals with an 80-yard drive resulting in a Michael Penix Jr. touchdown pass to Charlie Woerner . The scoring continued as they took a 10-7 lead later in the first quarter, but Cincinnati answered with 17 unanswered points in the second quarter and Atlanta never recovered. Penix finished 20-of-31 for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Bijan Robinson supplied the offense’s biggest bright spot with 100 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Drake London caught five passes for 68 yards, but Atlanta committed 12 penalties for 88 yards and allowed Joe Burrow to throw three touchdown passes. The central storyline from Atlanta’s perspective is will they be able to control the ball and keep Mahomes and co. off the field? The Falcons average 138.8 yards rushing per game. For Kansas City, it is about limiting Bijan Robinson and Atlanta’s rushing attack. The Chiefs have thrived against the run to date this season allowing just 96.3 yards on the ground per game. These teams last met two seasons ago. Mercedes-Benz Stadium was the site and Kansas City won 22-17. Mahomes threw for 217 yards and two touchdowns, while Rashee Rice caught 12 passes for 110 yards and a score; Atlanta, then quarterbacked by Kirk Cousins , had a chance late but could not complete the comeback. picks.headline: Chiefs-Falcons betting line & prediction: Will Josh Downs make instant impact?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs acquired receiver Josh Downs, who is expected to debut Sunday in Atlanta. Patrick Mahomes practiced fully Wednesday after an elbow injury scare vs. Jets. The betting line lists Kansas City as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta. The Kansas City Chiefs stopped a two-game losing streak Sunday with their 35-12 win over the New York Jets to improve to 6-2. Earlier Sunday, the Atlanta Falcons lost their second straight game, falling 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The loss dropped Atlanta to 3-6. How to watch Chiefs at Falcons Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -3.5 Behind the KC-ATL matchup The Chiefs and Falcons look a little different than they did last week, before the NFL’s trade deadline. Kansas City made the highly anticipated move Tuesday to acquire wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . Meanwhile, Atlanta began the week by agreeing to trade three-time second-team All-Pro safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars before sending starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens. Downs is expected to make his Chiefs debut Sunday in Atlanta. He recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown for the Colts this season. Downs’ stat line included seven catches for 72 yards against Kansas City in Week 2. “I had to watch him live. Yeah, which wasn’t good,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, drawing laughter from reporters. To earn extended playing time Sunday, Downs will have to demonstrate that he can handle Reid’s complex playbook. Kansas City kept that in mind while shopping for receivers. “That’s what we felt about Josh — that he has that ability,” Reid said. “And now it’s just a matter of him spending the time to knock it out. But he’s a pretty alert kid.” How Downs fits alongside Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy will be worth watching, but the good news for the Chiefs is that his debut should come with Patrick Mahomes under center. Mahomes suffered an injury scare late in the second quarter against the Jets. Mahomes hurt his elbow but remained in the game, and medical test results were encouraging. He was listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. In an encouraging development, Worthy (hamstring) also participated fully. “I feel like I’m in a great spot,” Mahomes said. “Now it’s just about pain and pain management and stuff like that, which I’ll try to do whatever I can to be in the best place possible.” While much of the focus will be on Downs’ Chiefs debut and how Mahomes attacks a Falcons secondary playing its first game without Bates, the path to victory is likely to look familiar. Running back Kenneth Walker presents a favorable matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 yards per carry. After two less productive games by his lofty standards, Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards against the Jets , adding four receptions for 41 yards and three total touchdowns. Following his breakout performance in Denver, rookie Emmett Johnson rushed for 34 yards and a touchdown on six carries against New York. Asked about the Falcons’ defense, Reid highlighted edge rusher James Pearce, who returned last week for 15 snaps after serving an eight-game suspension to begin the season. The former first-round pick registered 10.5 sacks as a rookie in 2025. Pearce (back) missed practice Wednesday, so his status is worth monitoring. “(The Falcons are) fast — and even faster when they’re on their turf,” Reid said. “So they’re very athletic. They’ve got some young linebackers that are flying around. They’ve got that front, and they rotate those guys.” With right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) out of practice Wednesday, Josh Ezeudu could be in line to make his second start of the season. Pearce can line up on either side of the line, and he will be a challenge for both Ezeudu and Chiefs left tackle Kahlil Benson. The Falcons feature 11 players with at least one sack, including defensive end Za’Darius Smith (4.5), defensive end Cameron Thomas (2) and defensive tackle LaCale London (2) — all with at least two sacks on the season. On offense, the Falcons’ biggest threat is running back Bijan Robinson, the only player in the league with more rushing yards (880) than Walker (872), though with one additional game. “He’s electricity in a bottle,” Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton said of Robinson. “That’s what I say. (He’s) able to change direction, get upfield, cutbacks. We see all the time everybody’s at the point of attack because he can cut it back and put pressure on the back-side corner on the outside zone to the opposite side. So he’s electricity in a bottle, like I said, and it’ll take all hands on deck.” Much like Kansas City, Atlanta wants its running game to create opportunities through the air. Robinson’s presence helps open things up for quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and wide receiver Drake London, who leads the Falcons with 692 receiving yards but only one touchdown. The Chiefs listed cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) as a full participant Wednesday, and his return after a two-game absence would help Kansas City match up against London. Kansas City’s defensive front will look to build on its momentum after sacking Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times last Sunday. Defensive end George Karlaftis and defensive tackle Chris Jones recorded two sacks apiece. According to NFL NextGen Stats, Penix posts a league-worst 34% completion percentage when under pressure. Jones should have an advantage over center Corey Levin, who is expected to make his first start of the season after replacing Neuzil. A sixth-round pick in 2017, Levin has spent most of his career in a reserve role. Despite kicker Harrison Butker’s recent struggles, Reid announced Wednesday that he would stick with him for now, with Justin Tucker waiting on the practice squad. Perhaps a homecoming for Butker, an Atlanta native, sparks the turnaround he’s been seeking. Chiefs-Falcons game prediction As evidenced by their respective deadline moves, the Chiefs are all in on 2026, as the Falcons look toward the future. Kansas City draws energy from Downs’ debut, Delane helps neutralize London and the pass rush builds on last week’s solid outing. Winner: Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 | Cover: Chiefs Sweeney’s record: (6-2-0) | Against the spread: (4-4-0) This story was originally published November 12, 2026 at 7:00 AM . away.headline: Josh Simmons: Ex-Chiefs OL refutes concerning report on 1st-round pick
away.blurb: Former Kansas City Chiefs star Mitchell Schwartz took to Twitter on November 12 to refute a report about injured offensive lineman Josh Simmons. During an appearance on 96.5 The Fan earlier in the day, ESPN writer Nate Taylor said that he hadn't seen Simmons around the Chiefs' facilities since Kansas City placed the former Ohio State Buckeye on its injured reserve list. Schwartz, on the other hand, has heard otherwise, tweeting that he had heard Simmons is "in the building" and "attacking rehab." Take a look at Schwartz's indirect refutation of Taylor's earlier report, which was posted to the All Pro lineman's Twitter account: The relative opacity that the Chiefs' front office, coaching staff, and trainers have maintained regarding Simmons' injury status will likely keep providing fodder for the rumor mill as Kansas City prepares for its highly anticipated Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 15. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers' league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who's allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud's other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston's lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns' permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that's going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he'll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That's a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland's defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Texans 22, Browns 19 Shedeur Sanders had 297 passing yards and two TDs in his first start of the season, and that might be enough to keep that in a home start against the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns' early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Huntington Bank Field. The Texans opened the season with four straight losses but have won three of their last four. The division may be out of reach as the Jaguars lead the Texans by three games in the AFC South but Houston is back in the race for a Wild Card spot. Cleveland takes the field after dropping their last two games which has dropped them out of first in the AFC North and 1.5 games behind the Steelers and the Bengals. Houston is coming off its most explosive performance of the season, a 44-22 road rout of the winless Los Angeles Chargers. C.J. Stroud played through an illness and completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. He connected with four different players for scores, including 63-yard touchdowns to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte , with Boutte finishing with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The Texans led 24-9 at halftime, stretched the advantage to 38-9 early in the fourth quarter and defensively overwhelmed Justin Herbert , sacking him eight times. Cleveland arrives home following a gut-wrenching 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. With Deshaun Watson sidelined by a concussion, Shedeur Sanders started and finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 64-yard go-ahead strike to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter. After New Orleans regained the lead, Andre Szmyt’s 51-yard field goal forced overtime. The Saints scored first in the extra period, but Sanders answered by finding Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown before Cleveland went for two and the win; the conversion failed, dropping the Browns to 5-4. The matchup also renews a surprisingly balanced series. Houston leads the all-time matchup 8-7, including the postseason, but Cleveland won four consecutive meetings from 2020 through the 2023 regular season. Their most recent clash reversed that trend in emphatic fashion: in the 2023 AFC Wild Card round, Stroud threw for 274 yards and three touchdowns as Houston demolished Cleveland 45-14, with the Texans turning two Joe Flacco interceptions into defensive touchdowns. In addition to Watson’s health, other storylines include the Texans’ pass rush against Cleveland’s quarterback protection particularly after Sanders was sacked five times in New Orleans and Houston just recorded eight sacks against the Chargers. away.headline: The Texans could be without their top running backs against Browns as Woody Marks misses practice
away.blurb: Running back Woody Marks, who practiced on a limited basis Wednesday, was not seen during the portion of practice open to the media on Thursday. The good news for Houston is that David Montgomery is nearing a return. He practiced Thursday for the first time since suffering a groin injury against the Titans several weeks ago. "David Montgomery is going through the process," Ryans said. "Still, he's getting better. We're encouraged by his progress so far. We'll see when he's able to get back out on the field." The Houston Texans could be without one of their top offensive playmakers Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. Marks was listed with a knee injury. Starting left guard Keylan Rutledge, who has a shoulder stinger, also was absent. It's unclear whether either will miss Sunday's game, but neither practicing Thursday puts their availability in doubt. Players who miss the team's most strenuous practice of the week typically don't play Sunday. Marks' absence would be a major blow to a Texans running game that already is struggling and ranks 29th in the NFL in rushing yards. Marks is coming off his best game of the season. He rushed for 70 yards last week in a 44-22 win over the Chargers. Ryans said Wednesday that the team was pleased with Montgomery's progress but that he wasn't sure whether Montgomery would play Sunday. If neither Marks nor Montgomery can play, new acquisition Emari Demercado likely will start against the Browns. The Texans claimed Demercado off waivers last month. He had 16 yards on six carries last week. The Browns rank 29th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed. The Texans are expected to try to establish the run Sunday. Temperatures at kickoff are forecast to be around 46 degrees, with a 20% chance of rain and winds of 12 mph, according to weather reports. Those conditions could make it difficult to throw. away.headline: Texans Injury Report vs. Browns Week 10: Multiple Starters Miss Practice
away.blurb: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans made it known that Montgomery's status has improved from last week ––when he was ruled out with a groin injury on Wednesday––but said he would continue to be evaluated throughout the week. It remains to be seen if he ends up playing once the weekend rolls around. Azeez Al-Shaair might be a name to keep an eye on, as he was a DNP with seemingly the same groin injury that's restricted his availability in practice as of late . However, given that he also had a personal designation, there's a better chance that he'll be good to go for either Thursday or Friday's session. Tight end Brevin Jordan also wound up as a DNP in practice with a finger/foot issue. If he's unable to go against the Browns, Houston has four other tight ends on the roster to turn to instead, including second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who was active on the gameday against the LA Chargers for the first time since Week 4. The Texans' final status for everyone on the roster will become clearer after Friday's practice. But until then, keep a close watch on those four who didn't practice, while also not losing sight of anyone who was limited for Wednesday’s action. home.headline: The Texans could be without their top running backs against Browns as Woody Marks misses practice
home.blurb: Running back Woody Marks, who practiced on a limited basis Wednesday, was not seen during the portion of practice open to the media on Thursday. The good news for Houston is that David Montgomery is nearing a return. He practiced Thursday for the first time since suffering a groin injury against the Titans several weeks ago. "David Montgomery is going through the process," Ryans said. "Still, he's getting better. We're encouraged by his progress so far. We'll see when he's able to get back out on the field." The Houston Texans could be without one of their top offensive playmakers Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. Marks was listed with a knee injury. Starting left guard Keylan Rutledge, who has a shoulder stinger, also was absent. It's unclear whether either will miss Sunday's game, but neither practicing Thursday puts their availability in doubt. Players who miss the team's most strenuous practice of the week typically don't play Sunday. Marks' absence would be a major blow to a Texans running game that already is struggling and ranks 29th in the NFL in rushing yards. Marks is coming off his best game of the season. He rushed for 70 yards last week in a 44-22 win over the Chargers. Ryans said Wednesday that the team was pleased with Montgomery's progress but that he wasn't sure whether Montgomery would play Sunday. If neither Marks nor Montgomery can play, new acquisition Emari Demercado likely will start against the Browns. The Texans claimed Demercado off waivers last month. He had 16 yards on six carries last week. The Browns rank 29th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed. The Texans are expected to try to establish the run Sunday. Temperatures at kickoff are forecast to be around 46 degrees, with a 20% chance of rain and winds of 12 mph, according to weather reports. Those conditions could make it difficult to throw. home.headline: Cleveland Browns Practice Report for Thursday November 12 Week 10
home.blurb: Browns rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston is dealing with a toe injury which has kept him out of practice both Wednesday and Thursday. That’s a bit concerning, as his status is looking a bit murky for Sunday. Boston has managed 32 receptions with team highs of 60 targets, 507 receiving yards and 15.8 yards per reception. He has also found the end zone three times. On the defensive side of the ball, safety Ronnie Hickman Jr. remains in the concussion protocol, and he has been able to do nothing in the past couple of days. He also remains a huge question mark for Sunday’s tilt. If Hickman cannot go, Daniel Thomas could see a start, with Donovan McMillan factoring in. However, the latter was the player added to the injury list with a hip, causing him to be a limited participant in practice Thursday. Last, but certainly not least, fullback Michael Burton did not practice for a second straight day due to a calf injury. Nine Browns Listed as Limited Participants We mentioned McMillan above, but eight other players were a limited participant on both Wednesday and Thursday at practice. Offensive tackle Tytus Howard (knee), center/offensive guard Elgton Jenkins (knee), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (wrist, ankle), cornerback Denzel Ward Jr. (quadriceps) and linebacker Quincy Williams (hamstring) round out the list. The Cleveland Browns are off the practice field at the CrossCountry Mortgage campus in Berea, wrapping up the second official practice of the week on Thursday afternoon ahead of the Week 10 clash with the Houston Texans. There were 11 players listed on the practice report with injuries after Wednesday’s session, and one player was added to the list after Thursday’s practice. In addition, nothing really changed from Wednesday, with just one player showing some improvement with an injury situation. Let’s dive in. Three Players Unable to Practice on Thursday our participation report from Thursday’s practice https://t.co/PwSEJFJnAf Rookie offensive tackle Austin Barber is nursing a calf injury, while defensive tackle Maliek Collins is battling an elbow issue. Tight end Harold Fannin Jr., who had the highlight-reel touchdown in overtime in Week 9 at New Orleans , is nursing a groin injury. He is second on the team with 453 receiving yards and a team-best four touchdowns, while he is tied with rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion with a team-best 37 receptions. Fannin’s status is one to watch closely.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset. … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20 Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close.
