(Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christopher Gates · SB Nation Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:13 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division's basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don't like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday's game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that's just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don't do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

picks.headline: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Sources: Mauricio Pochettino leaving USMNT for Manchester United TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justis Mosqueda · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:40 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers (6-3) are set to be three-point favorites over the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in Week 10, according to FanDuel's numbers . That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they'll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We'll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it'll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they've been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

picks.headline: Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers
picks.blurb: Week 10 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Kirk Cousins returns to lead Vikings vs. Packers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Sources: Mauricio Pochettino leaving USMNT for Manchester United TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, November 12, 2026 at 1:48 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It wasn't that long ago that Kirk Cousins, in his first stint with the Minnesota Vikings, was the quarterback who could never win the big one . Everyone remembers this critique of him. These days, Kirk Cousins is 38. And somehow, everyone spent days and weeks arguing that the only way for the Vikings to have a chance to win the big one was to trade for Cousins. That trade did happen, and it was perfectly reasonable for the Vikings to see if Cousins can guide them to an NFC North title and maybe a playoff run. They have the defense for it but we saw on Monday night that the offense was beyond repair with the quarterback situation they had. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was hesitant to announce Cousins would start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, but the Vikings didn't trade for Cousins to watch Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz start in a huge divisional game. While the trade for Cousins was reasonable, the Vikings still have the fourth-best quarterback in the division and the fourth-best offense in the division as well. Cousins is an upgrade but mostly because the Vikings had a dreadful quarterback situation. The Packers didn't do anything at the trade deadline but it might be because they've been on quite a roll. They were not good through three weeks but somehow have emerged as one of the better teams in the NFL since then. Since Week 4, they're fourth in EPA ( expected points added ) per play on offense and third in EPA per play allowed on defense. It's a good team. Anyone will have issues with the Vikings' defense and we'll see if the Packers' deep passing game can function against Minnesota's many blitzes. But Packers -3 is the pick. Taking the Vikings and Cousins, five days after rejoining the team, against a red-hot team is too much to ask. New Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) shown facing the Packers in a 2023 game. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 10 of the NFL season: Commanders (+2.5) over Giants The Giants are three games up on the Commanders in the NFC East, but New York isn't that great. The Commanders come in as the more desperate team. Their season is all but over if they lose on Thursday. That's not the best reason to pick a team, but it's good enough in a game between two flawed teams. Patriots (+2.5) over Lions This is the NFL's last early-morning game of the season. The Lions and Patriots meet in Germany. The Patriots are coming off a bad loss to the Packers, and have their running back issues with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson out. One factor to consider is the Lions aren't the same team outdoors. Jared Goff's rating in domes is 102.9 and outdoors it is 92.4. There is some noise in those numbers, and Goff's ratings haven't had that big of a gap the past two seasons, but Detroit also just scored 19 points at Miami last week. That and the Lions' defensive deficiencies are enough to take the Patriots and the points. Texans (-4.5) over Browns The Browns have a better record, but also a -35 point differential. It's not like the Texans have been great, but there's a path for them to make the playoffs. They also know they can't drop games like this one. C.J. Stroud is playing well enough that points shouldn't be too hard for Houston to come by. Titans (+10.5) over Jaguars The Jaguars have taken over as my Super Bowl pick after the deadline. However, 10.5 is a lot of points in the NFL and the Titans have played three close games in a row. They're coming off their bye and have some extra rest. The Jaguars can't blow everyone out, right? Colts (-3.5) over Dolphins It's very hard to take the Colts, especially because the Dolphins are playing hard. The Colts played hard last week, but have to be deflated after losing that game to the Cowboys in the final minutes and seeing more players traded away. But it's even harder to back new Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick who has never taken an NFL snap, playing with a subpar group. McCord gets the start for Miami with Malik Willis on injured reserve. Jets (+8) over Bills Talk about an ugly NFL side to take. The Jets are not good. But the Bills are coming off a physical game in Minnesota on Monday night and now go on the road to face the Jets on short rest. It seems unwise to take the Jets, but point spreads exist for a reason. Panthers (+2.5) over Saints The Saints are probably better in theory than reality. They won last week, but needed to defend a two-point conversion in overtime to knock off Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. It feels like the Saints have the potential to be the best team in the NFC South, but there's not much evidence they are. The Panthers are in a slump but have been the better team. Chiefs (-3.5) over Falcons It's not like the Falcons trading Jessie Bates III makes them significantly worse, but it's a difficult message for the locker room. It makes it seem like the front office is waving the white flag. In reality they got an offer they couldn't turn down, but it's still worth wondering how the remaining players will react. And Kansas City is a pretty good team. Cardinals (+9.5) over Rams For the rest of the season, or at least until Puka Nacua or Davante Adams returns, the Rams will try to survive by running the ball and playing defense in low-scoring games. There's not much explosiveness in the offense without any dangerous receivers. That will make them tough to back when the spread is large. Can Carson Beck lead the Arizona offense to enough points against a good Rams defense to cover any spread? That's the key question. Seahawks (-6.5) over Raiders This isn't a pick due to Fernando Mendoza facing the Seahawks defense, though that is a factor. It's because the Raiders defense is horrible. Since Week 3, after the Raiders had faced the offensively challenged Dolphins and Chargers, they're last in the NFL in EPA by a wide margin. They're 32nd in yards allowed and points allowed. The Seahawks will be able to move the ball, even with Drew Lock at quarterback. 49ers (-4.5) over Cowboys There are no signs the Cowboys are ready to have some kind of breakout. Last week they almost lost to a Colts team that has already given up on the season. And now they're supposed to keep it close against the 49ers, who have arguably been the best team in the NFL? Steelers (+3.5) over Bengals The Joe Burrow-for-MVP bandwagon is still running , but it's hard to lay more than a field goal in what should be a great divisional game. The Steelers can run the ball, and run defense is a weakness of the Bengals. They're last in the NFL in yards allowed per carry. Also, the Steelers are coming off a bye while the Bengals are coming off a game in Paris, which is the type of massive rest disadvantage that the NFL should do a better job avoiding. The Bengals are good but this isn't a great matchup or a good spot for them. Ravens (-4.5) over Chargers The Chargers will cover a spread this season. They haven't yet. They are the last team in the NFL to not cover the spread this season. But we'll take that loss when it comes because proactively taking the truly miserable Chargers in hopes they finally cover is not an enjoyable exercise. Also, the Ravens have three days of extra rest and perhaps a little bit of renewed hope with Jacoby Brissett coming aboard. Last week: 9-6 Season to date: 62-71-2

away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. home.blurb: Micah Parsons Predicts a Big Return After Months of Patience That teamwork is the next step in a gradual ramp-up. Parsons stuck to individual drills in his first practice back, but this week opened with an illness added to his injury designation, though he was still listed as a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice. How the Practice Window Shapes the Timing of Parsons’ Return Micah Parsons is in his second week of practice since tearing his ACL, and the Green Bay Packers edge rusher is already aiming high. On Thursday afternoon, Parsons made a confident six-word prediction in reply to a post showing him at practice. It came a day after coach Matt LaFleur, when asked whether Parsons would get 11-on-11 reps this week, replied, “That is the plan.” The post Parsons answered came from Dov Kleiman, who shared a look at him on the practice field and asked: “Micah Parsons at practice. What do you notice?” Parsons passed it along with his own answer: “That’s he gonna shock the world!” Getting to this point took nearly 11 months. Parsons tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee during a Week 15 loss to the Denver Broncos on December 14. He worked through the rehab with trainer Nate Weir, and his first practice since the injury came on November 4. That day, he summed up what the wait had asked of him: “Oh, my patience is amazing. I think I got the most patience than, you know, anyone. … It’s nothing but patience.” “I’m not going to be the All-Pro Micah, the person that, you know, I once was this year,” Parsons said. “Probably not until later, after I go through all my phases and things like that.” SEE THIS WEEK’S INJURIES: PFN’s NFL Injury Report He paired that caution with a picture of what he does expect people to see once he is back in games: “But I think what people will see is they’re going to see, like, this guy is ready to play football. And he’s going to play hard and he’s going to help boost his defense. And I think you’ll see flashes of All-Pro Micah when I get the pass rush. And there’s going to be times when you’re like, dang, what was Micah doing?” That All-Pro version is the one Parsons measured himself against. The four-time All-Pro recorded at least 12 sacks in each of his first five NFL seasons, the last of them after Green Bay acquired him from the Dallas Cowboys 10 days before the 2025 opener. In the 2025 NFL season, Parsons ranked No. 17 in PFN’s Edge Rusher Impact Metric with a grade of 82.0. home.blurb: Although Jacobs will undergo surgery later this week and is already ruled out for Sunday’s matchup against the Minnesota Vikings, his potential recovery timeline is shorter than initially feared. Jacobs could return in as little as two to three weeks, giving Green Bay hope that he won’t need an extended absence. Josh Jacobs could return in 2-3 weeks after surgery An injured reserve designation would require Jacobs to miss at least four games. Avoiding that decision would give the Packers more flexibility and potentially allow their starting running back to return much sooner. Green Bay has its bye following the Vikings game, meaning part of Jacobs’ recovery period will overlap with a week when the team isn’t playing. Rapoport indicated that Jacobs could have a chance to return after the bye, depending on how his recovery progresses. The Green Bay Packers have received encouraging news regarding Josh Jacobs after the running back suffered a broken ring finger against the New England Patriots in NFL Week 9. MORE: Top 10 NFL teams: Rankings updated after trade deadline According to Rapoport, Jacobs could be back on the field within two to three weeks following surgery on his broken ring finger. The Packers are expected to make a decision Saturday on whether to place him on injured reserve, but that move is not guaranteed. The latest update is encouraging considering the uncertainty surrounding Jacobs after head coach Matt LaFleur initially declined to provide a recovery timeline. LaFleur confirmed that surgery was necessary after Jacobs struggled to grip the football following the injury. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 10 of 2026 NFL season Packers will be without Jacobs against Vikings Jacobs will miss Sunday’s divisional matchup against Minnesota, but the timing of the Packers’ upcoming bye could work in his favor. The Packers will need other running backs to step up in his absence. Kaleb Johnson, Pierre Strong Jr. and potentially MarShawn Lloyd could help handle the workload against Minnesota. For Packers fans, the biggest takeaway is that Jacobs may not be facing a lengthy absence. The possibility of a two-to-three-week recovery gives Green Bay reason for optimism, although the team’s Saturday decision on injured reserve will be an important development to monitor.

Some five years ago, St. Brown spoke to Sky Sports about the importance of his German heritage ahead of entering the NFL Draft. And now he gets to honour it by doing what he does best. His mother Miriam hails from Leverkusen and predominantly spoke to the Lions wide receiver and his two brothers in German growing up, while also taking them back to Europe each summer to spend time with their grandparents and play soccer. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. The south-most AFC South team sold off a ton of draft potential to make this happen, but the 6-2 team got a whole lot better as they sprint toward a hopeful Super Bowl appearance. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. FOX Sports already had Jacksonville listed as a top 10 defensive team in the NFL prior to these trades. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. But this Jaguars team has the AFC South in a headlock, and the 1-7 Titans simply don't have enough on paper to climb out of a double-digit projected loss in this one. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) head to Nissan Stadium on Sunday in full control of the AFC South for an afternoon game against the last place Tennessee Titans (1-7). The Jaguars have won five of their last six and are coming off consecutive blowout victories. The Titans were off last weekend but take the field having dropped two straight since recording their only victory of the season at Indianapolis back in mid-October. As is the case in most NFL games, the spotlight shines the brightest on the quarterbacks as we approach gameday. Trevor Lawrence is flourishing having thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and only four interceptions. He is an MVP candidate. Tennessee’s Cam Ward continues to labor under center having thrown for 1,483 yards with only six touchdowns and yet five interceptions. His future with Tennessee looks uncertain. Jacksonville’s latest performance was a convincing 33-10 Thursday-night victory at Baltimore, its second straight win by at least 23 points. Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and delivered the game’s biggest offensive play, a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington late in the second quarter that sent Jacksonville into halftime ahead 17-3. The Jaguars limited Baltimore to 227 total yards, forced three turnovers and kept the Ravens out of the red zone entirely; Baltimore’s only touchdown came on a 65-yard Justice Hill run in the fourth quarter with Jacksonville already leading 33-3. As noted earlier, Tennessee had its bye last week. It came at an ideal time after an exhausting 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati, arguably its best offensive showing of the season despite another defeat. The Titans jumped ahead 13-0 and took a 36-29 advantage with just 3:46 remaining when Ward hit Wan’Dale Robinson for a 15-yard touchdown and converted the ensuing two-point try, but Cincinnati tied the game with 1:17 left and won in overtime on Joe Burrow’s nine-yard touchdown run. Ward produced his first career 300-yard passing game, completing 26 of 40 for 304 yards and two touchdowns, while Tony Pollard ran 21 times for 117 yards and two scores. Tennessee accumulated 440 yards and forced four turnovers, including three interceptions by safety Amani Hooker , yet its defense was shredded for 510 yards and allowed Burrow to throw for 462 yards and five touchdowns before his overtime rushing score. The rivalry adds another layer because Jacksonville has emphatically reversed what was once a Tennessee-dominated series. The Titans still lead 35-28 all time, including their famous 33-14 victory over Jacksonville in the 1999 AFC Championship Game, but the Jaguars have won four consecutive meetings and seven of the last 10. Jacksonville swept Tennessee in each of the past two seasons, including a 25-3 win in Nashville last November and a 41-7 rout in Jacksonville on Jan. 4, 2026, the largest Jaguars victory in the history of the rivalry. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Jacksonville Jaguars, matchups, prediction NFL Week 10
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Jacksonville Jaguars, matchups, prediction NFL Week 10 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Nov. 11, 2026, 5:02 a.m. CT With a 1-7 record, the Titans' focus for the rest of the season is on player evaluation. The Jacksonville Jaguars lead the AFC South and have strengthened their defense with recent trades. Trading Jeffery Simmons changed everything. The Tennessee Titans quietly submitted to a lost 2026 NFL season by dealing their eighth-year All-Pro defensive tackle to the Chicago Bears on Oct. 29. Tennessee general manager Mike Borgonzi then reinforced the team's desire to build for the future by trading eighth-year veteran safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 10. Barring a miraculous playoff push without their top two defenders, rivalry points seem to be all that matter for the Titans (1-7) in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15 (noon CT, FOX). The Titans’ final nine-game stretch will be about observations. Will quarterback Cam Ward play more like a franchise quarterback to finish his second season? Will star rookies Carnell Tate and Anthony Hill Jr. maintain their pace? Who are becoming pieces for Borgonzi’s long-term vision? Finding a way to win one-score games — the Titans have lost six — can help answer those questions regardless of the team’s final record. The Jaguars have won five of their past six games and have a three-game lead in the AFC South. They enhanced their defense this week by trading for All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and 10th-year defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Jaguars. One Jacksonville Jaguars stat to know: 28 That’s career interceptions for Bates. He’ll be a factor. He has at least one interception in each of his nine NFL seasons. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Jaguars Is Ward really the Titans’ only hope? He takes a lot of criticism, some deserved. But why can’t he be an advantage this time? He played at an elite level with a career-high 304 yards passing and two TDs against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. A Ward hot streak in November may be Tennessee’s best chance. The Jaguars rank 21st in the league in passing yards allowed per game (229.0). That’s one spot lower than Cincinnati. There’s an opportunity for Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll to give Ward more downfield throws as he did against the Bengals. Where Jacksonville Jaguars have edge vs. Titans Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence could have a big day against the Titans’ secondary, which was already leaky and now lacks its best player in Hooker. Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals shredded Tennessee with 462 yards passing, three touchdowns and nine plays of 18 yards or more. He was intercepted three times, but all of those came from Hooker. Aside from Alontae Taylor's solid debut at nickel cornerback against the Bengals, other parts of the secondary displayed poor tackling and bad angles. Tennessee ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed (258.3). Lawrence has thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. He's first in the league with 8.6 yards per pass among active quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Jaguars receiver Parker Washington has 493 yards on 29 catches and is ninth among league receivers with five touchdowns. He ranks third at 17 yards per catch. Matchup to watch Titans defensive end Jacob Martin versus Jaguars left tackle Walker Little. Martin is Tennessee’s best pass rusher with Simmons gone. He had three sacks against the Bengals and has 6.5 for the season. The Jaguars have shuffled their left tackle spot this season. Little has made only three starts, but he didn’t allow a single pressure or sack in last week’s 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Score prediction: Jaguars 28, Titans 21 Ward and the Titans' offense will maintain their recent progress. But Tennessee's inability to finish games will also continue. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? Reach him at tpalmateer@tennessean.com and on the X platform, @tpalmateer83 . He said that he didn't get to see whether he cut their hand or not. Ridley claimed that the attendant said that he broke their finger. "No, I didn't have the ticket," Ridley said. I gave them the registration after I got the keys. My wife came down. We got in the truck and left." Ridley was rumored to be moved ahead of the trade deadline . It was during the second half of Sunday Night Football. News broke that there was an incident at the Nashville Airport involving Titans receiver Calvin Ridley . We didn't learn exactly what happened until later. It was revealed that Ridley got upset with a valet attendant at the airport after trying to get his car keys back from them. The valet lost his ticket and refused to give him the keys since they couldn't identify his vehicle without it. It is worth noting that neither Davis or Bates have had bye weeks to this point, while the Jaguars have already had their bye week in Week 7. If Bates and Davis were to play every game for the Jaguars the rest of the way, each will have played 18 games in the regular-season, which doesn't even account for the likely playoff games that will come later. Well, technically. The Colts, 2-7, could claim the top spot, but they do not own their own first-round for the next draft, with the New York Jets holding that selection as part of an in-season trade last year that sent cornerback Sauce Gardner to Indianapolis. Despite the Dolphins' positive signs of growth over the past several weeks, the oddsmakers have given the Colts a slight nod in this game. The FanDuel Sportsbook line opened with Indianapolis favored by 2.5 points , slightly under the typical three-point advantage given to a home team, and it has remained steady as of Tuesday morning. If the Colts do start making trades ahead of the 4 p.m. Eastern deadline, how will the line move? Miami could also be sellers, with teams reportedly interested in players like linebacker Jordyn Brooks and defensive tackle Zach Sieler. The Dolphins may not be eager to move on from core pieces of their rebuild, but they may be offered a package of draft picks they cannot refuse. Tuesday could significantly affect the odds for this weekend's game, but for now, the Colts are slightly favored.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Miami Dolphins (1-7) and Indianapolis Colts (2-7) meet Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium in a matchup between two teams racing towards the top of the 2027 Draft. The Dolphins have lost two straight and sit in the cellar in the AFC East while the Colts have lost five in a row and have only the Titans between them and a spot in the basement in the AFC South. The headline as these teams take the field is that Miami’s starting signal-caller, Malik Willis , has been placed on the IR and as a result, rookie Kyle McCord will get the first start of his career. Indianapolis will continue with Daniel Jones , who has 1,722 passing yards and six touchdowns this season. Jones, however, has struggled to regain the form he had prior to tearing his Achilles late last season. Miami’s latest setback was a 19-9 home loss to the Detroit Lions, a game in which the Dolphins’ defense did enough to give the offense a chance but Miami never reached the end zone. Willis completed just 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards with an interception, while Ollie Gordon II led the Dolphins with 55 rushing yards and Caleb Douglas caught six passes for 70 yards. Miami finished with only 228 total yards, went 0-for-3 in the red zone and settled for three Zane Gonzalez field goals. Indianapolis’ last loss was considerably more painful. The Colts rallied from a 17-7 halftime deficit against Dallas, getting a 55-yard touchdown catch from Ashton Dulin and field goals of 59 and 50 yards from Spencer Shrader to take a 23-20 lead with 1:37 remaining. But Dak Prescott immediately hit Ryan Flournoy for 46 yards, and Javonte Williams scored from a yard out with 1:08 left to give Dallas a 27-23 victory. Jones finished 20-of-34 for 180 yards, a touchdown and an interception, while Jonathan Taylor managed only 46 yards on 13 carries and lost a costly fourth-quarter fumble. Dallas piled up 508 yards to Indianapolis’ 271, illustrating the biggest concern for a Colts’ team that is allowing 361.8 yards and 27.7 points per game. The central storyline, then, is which struggling offense can take advantage of an accommodating opponent. Miami is averaging only 15.8 points per game, 31st in the league, and will be asking McCord to make his debut on the road; Indianapolis averages 20.4 points but carries a -11 turnover differential, making ball security especially important for Jones and Taylor. Recent history favors the Colts. Indianapolis has won the last three meetings, including a 33-8 rout at Lucas Oil Stadium in Week 1 of the 2025 season, when Jones completed 22 of 29 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown and Taylor rushed for 71 yards. The broader history belongs to the Dolphins, who hold a 48-30 advantage across 78 regular-season and postseason meetings. 5 bold Colts predictions that could turn the Dolphins game upside down
picks.blurb: 5 bold Colts predictions that could turn the Dolphins game upside down Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites It’s been a roller-coaster of a year for the Indianapolis Colts. The team entered the season with hopes of contending for a division title, but now finds itself in a full-on rebuild. In the last few weeks, the Colts have fired their general manager, traded away key players, and lost five straight games. At this point, expecting any good news for Indianapolis would qualify as a “bold prediction”. But, the Colts have a chance to stop the bleeding in Week 10 when they host the 1-win Miami Dolphins — one of the only teams that’s just as much of a disaster as them. This is the perfect opportunity for Indianapolis to prove that they are still a competent football team that hasn’t forgotten how to win games. While it may be hard to believe, the Colts’ offense and defense may not look totally hopeless against the Dolphins this week. 5 bold predictions for the Indianapolis Colts Week 10 matchup with the Dolphins 1. Jonathan Taylor finally rushes for over 100 yards Shockingly, an entire year has passed since star running back Jonathan Taylor last crossed 100 rushing yards in a game. Of course, the issue isn’t a lack of talent, but the dysfunctional state of the entire Indianapolis offense. Even Taylor isn’t immune to that. This season, Taylor has run for over 90 yards five times, before just falling short of the elusive 100-yard mark. Against Miami, the conditions could be perfect for a big performance from Taylor. The Colts shouldn’t be playing from behind and can lean on him all game. A full workload against a mediocre defense is exactly what Taylor needs to break his 16-game curse. 2. Tyler Warren bounces back The Indianapolis wide receiver room has been decimated. Alec Pierce is still on Injured Reserve , while Josh Downs and Keenan Allen were traded on deadline day earlier this week. Those were the Colts’ top three wideouts entering the season, and none of them will be on the field in Week 10. Someone has to step up and fill the void. It’s been a quiet season for tight end Tyler Warren, who hasn’t been able to keep up his rookie-year momentum. Given the lack of proven pass-catching options in Indianapolis, Warren is poised to have a bounce-back game against the Dolphins. The Colts will likely target him early and often this week. Expect Warren to embrace his newly expanded role. 3. Indianapolis pass rush dominates After struggling for most of this season, the Colts’ pass rush has looked better recently with back-to-back-to-back three-sack games. Young playmakers Adetomiwa Adebawore, Laiatu Latu, and JT Tuimoloau have all stepped up. Now, the unit faces a team that has already allowed 21 sacks through seven games. On top of that, hyper-mobile Miami QB Malik Willis will miss the game due to injury, meaning second-year pro Kyle McCord is slated to make his NFL debut. McCord doesn’t have Willis-level speed to escape the pocket. He has also never played a regular season snap, so this will be his first time facing an NFL-level pass rush. Indianapolis’ recent success generating pressure, combined with Miami’s unfortunate QB situation, sets the stage for the Colts’ first 4+ sack performance of 2026. 4. Ollie Gordon has the best game of his career Indianapolis has the third-worst run defense in the league, allowing 137 rushing yards per game. Now, they face Miami running back Ollie Gordon, who has impressed in his second NFL season after taking over for the injured De’Von Achane. Gordon ran for a career-high 103 yards back in Week 7, but has a chance to set a new personal record against the Colts. Multiple running backs have had monster stat lines against Indianapolis this season, including Derrick Henry, Kenneth Walker III, Jaylen Warren, Bhayshul Tuten, and Javonte Williams. Gordon could easily join that group this week. 5. Colts end their five-game losing streak For the last five weeks, Indianapolis has been in a downward spiral with seemingly no end in sight. The losses are piling up and, after a series of trades, the Colts are now playing with a skeleton crew. It’s hard to imagine this group racking up many more wins before the end of the year. That being said, Week 10 will be Indianapolis’ best shot at victory in a long time. The Dolphins have only won once all year and are starting a backup QB this week. There is no such thing as an easy win for this version of the Colts, but a matchup against Miami and McCord is the closest thing to it. Indianapolis should be able to break their losing streak and hopefully breathe new life into their season. away.blurb: The good news for the Miami Dolphins with their final injury report for Week 9 is they didn't rule out any players for the matchup against the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium. The team did list three players as questionable and it might require some roster juggling Saturday. In fact, it probably will require it. The three players listed as questionable were running backs Jaylen Wright and Kaytron Allen, both of whom are dealing with a quad injury, and defensive end Malik Herring, who has a neck issue after sustaining a stinger in the Week 8 loss against the New England Patriots. It's also possible the Dolphins don't have to do anything beyond elevating Gonzalez if the three players listed as questionable are deemed fit and ready to go against Detroit before the deadline. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Carolina Panthers (3-5) and the New Orleans Saints (3-5) have each struggled mightily at times this season and yet they meet Sunday in the Bayou improbably tied atop the NFC South despite each having lost five of their eight games. Carolina has lost three straight after falling 26-21 to Denver, while New Orleans has won two of its last three and is coming off a 23-22 overtime victory over Cleveland. Carolina’s skid reached three games last Sunday against the Broncos, 26-21. A bright spot was the improved play of Bryce Young who completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Chuba Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and Darren Waller caught eight passes for 90 yards. Carolina finished with 353 total yards and averaged 4.8 yards per rushing attempt but couldn’t turn that production into a win. The Panthers statistical profile underlines their issues. They average 24.9 points and 362.4 yards per game, including 261.1 through the air, but Carolina surrenders roughly 27 points per game. New Orleans comes in with considerably more momentum after surviving last Sunday in Cleveland, knocking off the Browns 23-22 in overtime. QB Tyler Shough helped erase a fourth-quarter deficit and then directed a 74-yard touchdown drive to open overtime, finishing it with a 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson . The New Orleans defense generated five sacks, with Carl Granderson getting two. The win was the Saints’ first home win of the season. This rivalry has been remarkably competitive historically, although New Orleans has controlled it recently. The Saints swept Carolina last season and now lead the all-time series 34-29, including their lone postseason matchup. Their most recent meeting came last season on December 14, in New Orleans, when the Saints upset the Panthers 20-17 on Charlie Smyth’s 47-yard field goal with two seconds remaining. away.blurb: Carolina opened the 21-day practice windows on Wednesday for cornerback Mike Jackson, wide receiver Xavier Legette and running back Jonathon Brooks to return from injured reserve. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, guard Damien Lewis and cornerback Will Lee III returned to practice after missing time with injuries, while versatile offensive lineman Brady Christensen entered his second week in the 21-day practice window and is nearing his return. Coach Dave Canales said it's too early in the week to know who'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Saints. The Panthers held a light practice on Wednesday, and Canales said he should know more later in the week once the medical staff is able to evaluate the injured players' progress. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 1:42 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their fourth straight game and seventh of their last eight on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They kept it competitve for a half. In the first half the Jets outgained the Chiefs. They won the turnover battle. They had more than twice the time of possession as the Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 – 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 – 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. Regardless, if the Jets don't exit next week with their eighth loss of the season it will be a major surprise. Join Gang Green Nation on game day! Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. Buffalo has won eight of the past 10 meetings, including a couple smacks last season, beating the Jets 30-10 at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 14, 2025 and 35-8 in Buffalo on Jan. 4, 2026. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. home.headline: New York Jets Sign 29-Year-Old Player After Loss to Chiefs
home.blurb: Drafted by the Atlanta Falcons in the fourth round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of Fresno State, Walker has played for four NFL teams over the course of his six seasons in the league. New York Jets Sign 29-Year-Old Player After Loss to Chiefs Unlock the latest Heavy on Jets news — direct to your inbox. The New York Jets fell to 2-7 on Sunday after suffering a 35-12 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. New York has now dropped four games in a row and has seemingly had a very busy Monday as it sets its sights on Week 10. The Jets agreed to trade six-year safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 sixth-round pick ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Not long after that, they made another notable roster move. Jets Sign 29-Year-Old Linebacker According to Connor Long of Jets X-Factor , the Jets are signing 29-year-old linebacker Mykal Walker to their practice squad. The move comes with Kiko Mauigoa still on injured reserve and Trevin Wallace currently dealing with an injury after missing Sunday's game against Kansas City. Walker is quite familiar with the Jets organization, as he appeared in 14 games for the team last year, primarily playing special teams and serving in a rotational defensive role. However, after roster cuts, the Jets ultimately released him with an injury settlement. NEWS: The #Jets are signing LB Mykal Walker to their practice squad, a source tells me. Walker appeared in 14 games for New York last season, contributing on defense and special teams. He was released with an injury settlement after roster cuts. — Connor Long (@connor_long15) November 9, 2026 He spent his first three seasons with the Falcons, appearing in 49 games and making 20 starts. In 2023, he joined the Pittsburgh Steelers before moving to the Washington Commanders in 2024 and ultimately landing with the Jets in 2025. Walker saw most of his production in Atlanta, but he has also made an impact with three other NFL teams. Across 88 career games and 30 starts, he has totaled 272 tackles, 14 pass deflections, eight tackles for loss, four interceptions and one sack. While nobody missed the team's walkthrough, several key contributors are managing injuries, including four offensive linemen who were listed as limited participants. Buffalo's first injury report of Week 10 includes six limited participants and five full participants. The team held a walkthrough on Wednesday, meaning the participation designations are estimates rather than the result of a full practice. The biggest area to watch remains along the offensive line. Alec Anderson, Spencer Brown, Dion Dawkins, and Connor McGovern were all limited Wednesday. Anderson and Brown were listed with ankle injuries, Dawkins with a rib injury, and McGovern with a neck injury. Christian Benford was also limited by a wrist injury. Seattle is coming off a quieter offensive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, but this matchup presents a chance for the Seahawks to get back on track in a big way. The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. Meanwhile, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first NFL start against a Seattle defense that has been one of the toughest units in the league. I expect the Seahawks to take advantage of both matchups. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 4: Jadarian Price scores his first NFL touchdown Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images This could finally be the game when Jadarian Price gets into the end zone for the first time in his NFL career. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. JSN is coming off a relatively quiet performance against the Cardinals, finishing with seven catches for 51 yards without a touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. picks.headline: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 tracker: Injury updates, prediction, storylines and more
picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 tracker: Injury updates, prediction, storylines and more - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Scores / Schedules Sources: Mauricio Pochettino leaving USMNT for Manchester United Story by Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 tracker: Injury updates, prediction, storylines and more Story by Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is seen before a game | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Lee Vowell · 12th Man Rising Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads About our Ads The Seattle Seahawks are 5-4 and head to Las Vegas to play the 4-5 Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Week 10. Seattle will be playing with a backup quarterback, Drew Lock, and Las Vegas will have a rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, in his first career start. Head coach Mike Macdonald's team still has the better roster, and should be expected to win, but the Raiders are better this season than in quite some time. A victory against Seattle would be huge for their collective confidence. Health could be a factor. Seattle's injury report was fairly lengthy, so even some players who perform in Week 10 might not be close to 100 percent. At least, the bye week follows in Week 11. Seattle Seahawks injury updates for Week 10 Anthony Bradford Charles Cross Ribs and quad Elbow and oblique Quenton Nelson Uchenna Nwosu Patrick O'Connell Connor O'Toole Personal matter Rashid Shaheed Jaxon Smith-Njigba Leonard Williams Sam Darnold has already been ruled out, so he won't play. Drew Lock was expected to be limited all week, but is expected to play in Week 10. Leonard Williams is already trending toward missing another game. He will be missed. Seattle will announce its full list of inactives an hour and a half before kickoff, and this article will be updated with the latest information. Raiders inactives and injury updates Thomas Booker Foley Fatukasi Shoulder and back Trey Zuhn III The Raiders are fairly healthy, but what doesn't show on their injury report is the trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. This means rookie Fernando Mendoza will start for the first time in the NFL. As with Seattle, Vegas will announce its inactives an hour and a half before kickoff. How to watch Seahawks vs. Raiders in Week 10 Date: Sunday, November 15 Time: 1:05 p.m. PT TV Network: CBS (KIRO 7 in Seattle) Announcers: Ian Eagle (play-by-play), Ross Tucker (analysis), and Evan Washburn (sideline reporter) In the Seattle area, you can also stream the game on NFL+, while nationally, you might need a subscription to YouTube TV's NFL Sunday Ticket to stream or watch the game. You can listen to the game on the Seahawks Mobile App, SiriusXM channels 123 or 269, Seattle Sports 710 AM, and KIRO Newsradio 97.3. Steve Raible will provide the play-by-play for the Seahawks broadcast, while Dave Wyman will do the analysis, and Jen Mueller will report from the sidelines. Storylines to watch for Seahawks in Week 10 How will Fernando Mendoza do? Obviously, what most national fans will be interested in is how well the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will do in his first career start . While Vegas trading Kirk Cousins made sense, Mendoza's first two starts couldn't come against tougher defenses: The Seahawks and then the Denver Broncos. Presumably, head coach Klint Kubiak isn't going to let Mendoza throw the ball 50 times, but he could have a somewhat conservative game plan to operate with. Kubiak is a good coach, so fans should expect a difficult challenge, even against a rookie quarterback. Will Drew Lock succeed against a non-Arizona Cardinals team? The difference between Lock games and Sam Darnold games has been significant this season. Lock has turned the ball over in three games. Darnold has nine interceptions in six games. What fans have seen from Lock might not be reality, though. He played the majority of reps in Week 1 against the New England Patriots, but Week 1s are often lies. His other two games have been against the terrible Cardinals. Darnold has faced far tougher competition. Lock's true first test might come against the Raiders, who are eighth in the league with seven interceptions. Can the Seahawks succeed running the ball? Week 9 against the Cardinals looked quite a bit different offensively for Seattle. That is partly because running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were healthier. To win with Lock, and even when Darnold returns, the running game needs to continue being good. The Raiders are tight for last in the NFL at allowing 5.0 yards per carry. They are also last in yards allowed per rushing attempt at 151.2. The Seahawks must run the ball effectively to win. Prediction for Week 10 Seahawks 21, Raiders 14 This game is difficult to predict due to a number of factors, including how good Mendoza might be and the overall health of the Seahawks' defense. If Leonard Williams and Uchenna Nwosu miss the game again, the normally lofty standard of Mike Macdonald's defense could be exposed by a good offensive coach for Las Vegas. The hope is that Seattle wins a fairly ugly game, one that will probably be close until the end. Hopefully, Drew Lock just plays another clean game. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Seattle Seahawks (5-4) head to Las Vegas on Sunday trying to establish some momentum in a tightly packed NFC West race, while the Raiders (4-5) are looking to rebound from one of their sloppiest performances of the season AND are looking to do so with rookie Fernando Mendoza making his first start of his career. The matchup is a monster challenge for Mendoza: Seattle has leaned on a defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth-best in the league entering the week, while Las Vegas has surrendered 29.8 per game, ranking last. So you expect the Raiders would look to lean on Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. to run the ball and take the pressure off their rookie signal-caller…but know that the Seahawks allow an average of 89.1 yards per game (151.2 for the Raiders). Quarterback is also a storyline for the Seahawks. Sam Darnold remains sidelined with a quad injury after also reportedly cracking a rib against Chicago, while Drew Lock came out of this past Sunday’s game dealing with an oblique issue after previously battling elbow tendinitis. Seattle comes in off a much-needed 17-3 victory over Arizona, a game it controlled despite playing without starting quarterback Darnold. Backup Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown, while tight end AJ Barner supplied both Seattle touchdowns, catching one from Lock and running for another. Zach Charbonnet , recently returned from an ACL injury, gave the offense some balance with 77 yards on 16 carries, and the defense held Arizona to 216 total yards and no touchdowns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught seven passes for 51 yards and became the first NFL receiver to reach 1,000 yards this season. Las Vegas, meanwhile, is trying to clean up the turnovers after a 38-17 loss at San Francisco dropped it below .500. The Raiders were actually within 21-10 at halftime, but Kirk Cousins was intercepted on the first play of the third quarter and Jaden Dugger returned it 35 yards for a touchdown, beginning a disastrous second half. Cousins finished 22-of-32 for 216 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions as Las Vegas committed five turnovers, managed only 240 total yards and 24 rushing yards, and possessed the ball for just 21:42. Brock Bowers was possibly the only bright spot, catching seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown. Sunday’s game is also a reunion of two franchises with considerably more history than their present-day conference alignment suggests. The Raiders and Seahawks were AFC West rivals from 1977 through 2001, and the Raiders lead the overall series 30-26, including postseason games. They have met only periodically since Seattle moved to the NFC, with the last meeting producing one of the wildest games of the 2022 season: the Raiders won 40-34 in overtime in Seattle, powered by Josh Jacobs’ 229 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Cross (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) did not practice Wednesday, and Macdonald has not made a decision on either. away.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday: Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

home.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday: Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

take on the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) Sunday in Glendale. The Rams’ struggles are the result of injuries and consistently inconsistent play. That said, they take the field riding a three-game winning streak that has pushed them into a tie with Seatle for second in the NFC West. The Cardinals are last in the division as a result of losses two of the last three weeks. Los Angeles has climbed back into the playoff chase behind Matthew Stafford , who has thrown for 2,374 yards and 16 touchdowns. Arizona averages only 19.8 points per game while surrendering 28.3, but there is one significant reason the Rams won’t take the Cardinals lightly: Arizona already beat them 18-16 on Oct. 18 at SoFi Stadium. Los Angeles extended its winning streak to three last Sunday with a 20-13 road victory over the Washington Commanders. The Rams’ defense has been central to the turnaround, holding the Chargers to nine points and Washington to 13 in consecutive weeks, and Los Angeles enters Sunday allowing only 20.1 points and 312.9 yards per game. The major concern is what Stafford will have around him. Star receiver Puka Nacua , the team’s leading receiver with 715 yards, is out after suffering knee and toe injuries, while Davante Adams remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and tight end Terrance Ferguson is also sidelined. It is up to Head Coach Sean McVay and Stafford to keep the offense functioning even with several of its most important weapons sidelined. Arizona’s most recent outing was far less encouraging. The Cardinals followed up a thrilling and improbable 33-30 overtime win in Dallas with a 17-3 loss at Seattle. The Cardinals are now 3-6 and, remarkably, 0-3 at home, while an offense already struggling for consistency is undergoing a major change at quarterback. With Gardner Minshew placed on injured reserve, rookie Carson Beck is set to make his first appearance against the Rams, putting even more importance on running back Tyler Allgeier and tight end Trey McBride , who leads Arizona with 598 receiving yards and five touchdown catches. The recent history makes this matchup particularly interesting because as noted earlier, Arizona has already pulled off one of the season’s bigger divisional upsets. On Oct. 18, the Cardinals went into SoFi Stadium and beat the Rams 18-16 despite failing to score a touchdown, riding six field goals from Chad Ryland . Los Angeles took a 16-15 lead with 46 seconds remaining on a Stafford touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson , only for Arizona to drive back into field-goal range and win on Ryland’s 43-yarder as time expired. That result interrupted what had otherwise been a Rams-dominated stretch in the rivalry: Los Angeles beat Arizona 45-17 in December 2025 and 37-20 in January 2026, and the Rams lead the complete series 53-42-2, including a 2-0 postseason record.
