home.blurb: Rams-Cardinals injury report: McDuffie, Curl and Ferguson DNP Wednesday - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks Rams-Cardinals injury report: McDuffie, Curl and Ferguson DNP Wednesday To start the week, the Rams listed 10 players on their initial injury report, five of whom did not practice at all. The Rams only held a walk-through, so participation is an estimate. Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl and Terrance Ferguson were all non-participants. Sean McVay said the Rams are "optimistic" McDuffie will be able to play on Sunday, which is a good sign despite his absence Wednesday. Curl played last week after being questionable with a foot injury, but he's now listed with a toe injury. Ferguson is dealing with a hamstring injury after pulling it in practice last week. He's still on IR but can be activated at any time. Colby Parkinson continues to battle a rib injury, but it's encouraging that he was at least limited on Wednesday. Joe Cardona could be making progress with his ankle injury, too. Myles Garrett continues to nurse his knee injury and Davis Allen has an oblique injury that forced him to be limited. On the Cardinals' injury report, Budda Baker had a rest day, and Hjalte Froholdt missed practice while recovering from a concussion. Bam Knight is still progressing through the concussion protocol and was limited in practice. Josh Sweat and Isaac Seumalo both got veteran rest days, too. picks.blurb: 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Sources: Mauricio Pochettino leaving USMNT for Manchester United TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge 49ers vs. Cowboys bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:03 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the San Francisco 49ers made a fairly mild move, the Dallas Cowboys didn't move the needle at the trade deadline. But these teams meet in Week 10 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Entering with a record of 7-1, the 49ers sit as the No. 1 in the NFC. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are trying to fight their way back into contention in the NFC East. They have a record of 4-5. The 49ers are road favorites, but only by 3.5 points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 250 yards and two TD passes It's a matter of scheme that Purdy will have success , according to ESPN. "Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas," Matt Bowen wrote. "Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense, allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road." Purdy has thrown for 1,980 yards this season with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has been impressive and has the eye of head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to a post on X by 95.7 TheGame via Heavy.com. "Yeah, it's been amazing," Shanahan said. "Just since the first game he got in there. That's why I struggle at the beginning of the year when everyone's asking me, can I believe how good he's playing and how much better he's improved because he was so good off the bench versus Miami in his first game and the second week… taking us to the NFC Championship as a rookie. "And I think his second year took us to the Super Bowl maybe. So Brock's been the man since he's come in, and it's pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started… very fortunate to have Brock." The Cowboys will have their hands full. Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb will get 8-plus catches and 90-plus yards The Cowboys are going to get the ball to Lamb. It's their best path to having a shot at beating the 49ers. Lamb left the win over the Colts with a sigh of relief, according to dallascowboys.com. "Those are the games that you love to end up on top," Lamb said. "We understand it was the same situation that we were kind of in last week, and we didn't end up on top then, so just finishing out the game, finishing out the drive — shout out to the defense for ending the game. "But I think I had, like, three penalties alone in the second half, and a fumble. Personally, I gotta take a real good look. The numbers look crazy, but it could have been more. And I'm always thinking about what could have been. So, as for me, as a leader on this offense,I feel like I've got to be better in some realms and just end the game." The 49ers are off to a great start. But before the season, the Cowboys were in the same conversation with them. Lamb said the Cowboys need to get the job done. "We know what we got going on, just the history of that [matchup], the guys that they have over there on defense and the prep, I mean, it's going to take a lot of a lot of preparation, and a lot of execution," Lamb said. "We can't have as many flags because they have a really good offense, too." Prescott will lean heavily on Lamb if George Pickens misses another game. But even if Pickens plays, Prescott won't forget who he needs to target, early and often. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey will get in the end zone twice Look for McCaffrey to score on the ground and with a reception. The 49ers are going to get him the ball near the goal line. One thing that helps McCaffrey's overall usage is that Shanahan is more confident that he is ready to rock after a pre-bye injury slowed him somewhat, according to ninerswire.com. "No. I actually forgot about it," Shanahan said. "He had a good bye week, and he told me before the bye week in Christian style not to worry about it at all. He'll be fine, and he looked good all week." McCaffrey hasn't had a blowout game all season. His rushing high is 75 yards, and his receiving high is 61. But he has 10 total touchdowns, with nine of them coming off the ground. And consistency has been a hallmark. McCaffrey has scored in seven straight games. In three of those contests, he scored twice. The 49ers will need to be sharp offensively. Despite the way their defense has played, they will have trouble slowing down the Cowboys' high-octane offense. McCaffrey will likely need those scores to keep his team in good business. away.headline: 49ers ignore age critics with ironic new slogan as injuries pile up
away.blurb: The 49ers are embracing their mature wide receiver room. After trading for Keenan Allen, San Francisco’s top three receivers are all 30 years or older. General manager John Lynch unknowingly created a new slogan for aging players in the NFL — 35 is the new 30. “I don’t think that’s like a conscious thing. We’re not saying let’s go find every old guy. We feel like it’s a good mix because we have those vets,” Lynch said on KNBR. “I do think there’s some level of 35 is the new 30, so these guys are taking such great care of themselves.” Ironically, the 49ers were originally interested in acquiring former Colts wide receiver Josh Downs, who is 25 years old. But San Francisco ultimately pivoted to the six-time Pro Bowler. Lynch revealed 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan wondering about Allen’s availability served as the catalyst for the trade getting done. “Kyle and I are kind of watching Josh [Downs] and in the process, Kyle’s like, ‘What about Keenan?’ I hadn’t given much thought to that, but then I’m like let me ask,” Lynch said. “It’s always fluid and at a certain time they didn’t want to give him up.” Indianapolis was initially reluctant to part ways with Allen, but the 49ers have now added another veteran to the wide receiver room. The 49ers wanted to have ample options at the position, which led to the trade for Allen. Lynch said the veteran is not an insurance policy for Mike Evans, who is dealing “We wanted to make an add there, nonetheless,” Lynch said. Nowadays, it seems like the requirement to be a 49ers wide receiver includes being in your 30s.

home.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys have put out their second injury report of the week ahead of the Week 10 game against the San Francisco 49ers. Three players were listed as limited, also, including wide receiver George Pickens, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and wideout KaVontae Turpin, all of whom didn't play last week. Turnpin has missed multiple games with his injury. Now, for some good news: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown was upgraded to full after being limited on Wednesday, so he's now trending toward playing. With Pickens being listed as limited once again, this keeps his status for Week 10 up in the air after Pickens was limited all throughout last week before being inactive. We'll see if Pickens is capable of turning in a full practice on Friday, but if not, he will likely be listed as questionable once again. Dallas Cowboys vs. Indianapolis Colts Inactives: Who's In, Who's Out For Week 9 George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr Among 7 Dallas Cowboys Questionable For Week 9 The Wednesday injury report was loaded, with 16 players listed on it, and six of those players, including cornerback Joey Porter Jr., didn't take part in practice for an injury-related reason. Now, let's see if any of those players were upgraded on Thursday. Cowboys' Thursday injury report Alijah Clark and Juanyeh Thomas are new additions to the injury report, but Clark only has an illness, so no real concern there. Overshown told reporters he expects to suit up on Sunday and went into detail about what happened with his hamstring. "It was just some ongoing stuff that we didn't... I ain't going to say properly address the first round, but it was just like the hamstring. It happens that you really don't know when it's all the way healed," Overshown said, per Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News. "So I was feeling good. And next thing you know, I got blood and fluid just clogged up in there," he added. "So that was something that we wasn't expecting, but the problem is fixed now and I'm ready to get back to it.” As for every other player on the injury report, it was status quo. Pickens missed a game last week for the first time since being traded to the Cowboys. Porter was a non-participant once again at practice on Thursday. Porter told Jon Machota of The Athletic that his foot is "jacked up," and he denied that his absences for the Cowboys this season have anything to do with his contract. “My goal is to win games and play football. If there’s any chance I can get on the field, I’m gonna get on the field and do what I do best," he said. The Cowboys will drop their final injury report on Friday, so we'll likely have a clearer picture of Porter's status then. But, at this moment, it looks like he's not going to play again. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers had one of his best games of the season, throwing for 292 yards, three scores and one pick to lead the Steelers to a win at home. Now, they find themselves as underdogs on the road out of their bye week agaist Joe Burrow and Co. The Bengals are on fire right now, knocking off the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid in Week 9 for their fourth win in a row. Burrow, who is now tied with Josh Allen in the odds to win the MVP award this season, has thrown 16 scores over the last four weeks and adding a rushing touchdown for good measure in the blowout win over Atlanta. Oddsmakers have given the Bengals the edge in this division, setting them as odds-on favorites to win it ahead of this Week 10 clash. While all the primetime games in Week 10 aren't great, this matchup on Sunday Night Football is expected to be a close one between two potential playoff teams. Steelers vs. Bengals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Steelers +3.5 (-110) Bengals -3.5 (-110) Steelers: +150 Bengals: -180 48.5 (Over -108/Under -112) Based on these odds (Cincy -180), the Bengals have an implied probability of 64.29 percent to get the win at home. This is a tough turnaround travel wise since the Bengals were in Madrid in Week 9, but they are 2-1 at home in the 2026 season. Meanwhile, the Steelers should be fairly healthy coming out of their bye week, and they have also won four games in a row to get to the top of the AFC North. Pittsburgh won the division in the 2025 season, and with the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns both losing in Week 9, this is shaping up to be a two-team race. Cincy has a fairly easy schedule the rest of the way, which is a big reason why oddsmakers have set it as the favorite in the division. “First off, we do believe the Bengals have the strongest path to win the division,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. “If you look at their schedule the rest of the way, it is quite soft. The [Kansas City] Chiefs game in Week 14 is the only game we project that they will not open as the favorite as things currently stand. They have two games against the Browns, [Indianapolis] Colts game, [Washington] Commanders game, and a Ravens game – which is a lot less daunting than it once was. So, all of those games look to be pretty bankable. “Whereas the Steelers really have a much rougher path. They've still got to play the [Denver] Broncos and the Jags (Jacksonville Jaguars). Their only real bankable wins are the [Tennessee] Titans, and then they get two Ravens games.” It'll be interesting to see if this line moves at all in the coming days, but it appears the Bengals are going to close as favorites as they look to split the season series with their AFC North rival. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Sources: Mauricio Pochettino leaving USMNT for Manchester United TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown Alex Frank · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:05 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is as big of a home game as it gets for the Cincinnati Bengals . It's mid-November, against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and first place in the AFC North is on the line. Both the Bengals and Steelers are 6-2 and have both won four straight games. Not to mention, these two teams have already played this season. It was in Week 3, with the Steelers winning 30-27 in Pittsburgh. Right now on FanDuel , the Bengals are 3.5-point favorites next Sunday night. The Bengals' moneyline is -200, while the Steelers' is at +168. The over/under is at 47.5. Sunday night could be an extremely physical game. It's an AFC North rivalry with sole possession of first place in the division at stake. Also, it's the Bengals and Steelers. That's all you need to know for the potential level of physicality. Pittsburgh stole the first game against the Bengals, aided by two Bengals turnovers in the fourth quarter that included Joe Burrow getting strip-sacked with the Bengals on the edge of field goal range in the final minute. The Bengals never ran an offensive play with the lead in that game, but there were some great performances from their star players. Joe Burrow was 28/37 for 282 yards and three touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase caught nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins hauled in six passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also caught a 25-yard touchdown on 4th&2 early in the fourth quarter. For the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns, while Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries. Eight different players caught a pass for the Steelers, with Darnell Washington leading the way with 67 receiving yards on three receptions. Roman Wilson, D.K. Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek each caught a touchdown for the Steelers. Rodgers currently has 1,871 passing yards and 13 touchdowns on the season, but he's also thrown six interceptions and is completing just 60.8 percent of his passes. Warren has 704 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Washington and fellow tight end Pat Friermuth lead the Steelers with three and four touchdowns, respectively. T.J. Watt, as of Sunday night, leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks, and he also has nine tackles for loss. Cornerback Jamel Dean also has three forced fumbles. Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt off the stat sheet in that game, which bodes well going into Sunday night. The Bengals' offense scored on five of their eight drives in the first meeting in Week 3, gaining 352 yards of offense and rushing for 83 yards on 18 carries. Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries.

picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Sources: Mauricio Pochettino leaving USMNT for Manchester United TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final (Sam Greene/The Enquirer / USA TODAY) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 11, 2026 at 11:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Joe Burrow accounts for four touchdowns for the fifth straight game Burrow is on a heater, scoring four or more touchdowns, whether throwing or running, in four straight games. In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. Earlier this season against the Bengals , Warren ran for the second-most yards of his season, with 127. Two weeks ago against Cleveland, Warren topped that number with 143 yards. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. A lot is at stake in this game, with the winner taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh doesn't have much momentum, especially on offense, as its best wide receiver, DK Metcalf, has been struggling with drops lately. He has just 378 receiving yards this season and has topped 100 yards just once, with a 115-yard day against Cleveland earlier this season. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

picks.headline: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash
picks.blurb: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash - Yahoo Sports Search query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Aryan Chadha · HITC Mon, 9 November 2026 at 11:30 am UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Premier League Scottish Football Champions League Europa League Club World Cup About our ads Mike Tomlin is expecting a blockbuster AFC North showdown between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals, backing both teams to deliver an entertaining contest with the division lead at stake. The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. "It's AFC North football and you know I love that. You can airmail me right to Cincinnati," Tomlin said. He also highlighted the individual battle that could define the game, with Joe Burrow and the Bengals passing attack facing Pittsburgh's formidable pass rush. "It's good on good. Joe Burrow and that Cincinnati passing game vs T.J. Watt and the four-man rush of the Steelers…. Bring your popcorn and get your cameras ready." Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers' four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. Tomlin will have a particularly interesting perspective from the NBC booth as he watches the Steelers take on a Bengals team that will be determined to settle the score on home turf. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images Frank Platko · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals 6-2 Cleveland Browns 5-4 Baltimore Ravens 4-5 Matchup: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers, 8:20pm EST The Bengals avoided a potential letdown game last week against the Atlanta Falcons in Spain, securing a 34-17 victory. After losing the first quarter by three points, the Bengals outscored the Falcons by 20 points for the remainder of the contest. Now riding a four-game win streak, having exceeded 30+ points in each game, the Bengals will return home for a primetime matchup with the Steelers. In Week 3, the Bengals suffered a 30-27 defeat against Pittsburgh and sit in second place now despite having the same record. Cincinnati's passing attack has been firing on all cylinders recently and Joe Burrow is hitting his stride. Over the last four games, Burrow has 16 touchdown passes while averaging over 300 passing yards. The Steelers are a Top 3 defense against the run but rank middle-of-the-pack defending the pass. The Bengals continue to struggle running the ball effectively, so they'll likely attack Pittsburgh's secondary regularly. Elsewhere, the Bengals' inconsistent run defense may be tested by Steelers' rushing attack that has totaled 148 yards and 200 yards on the ground in back-to-back games. The Bengals will need to slow down Jaylen Warren in the backfield, who has been a star this season. If the Bengals can make the Steelers one dimensional offensively, they become a much more beatable team. Matchup: vs. Cincinnati Bengals, 8:20pm EST Like their divisional counterpart, the Steelers have won their last four games to improve to 6-2, sitting atop the division by virtue of tiebreaker. Prior to last week's bye break, the Steelers defeated the Browns handedly by 21 points, their most lopsided win of the season and only their second win by more than one possession. Pittsburgh's momentum will be put to the test in a tough road environment this Sunday night with the AFC North lead on the line. The Steelers have won the turnover battle in three consecutive games. That will be an important factor for them to defeat the Bengals. Burrow has taken good care of the ball this year but did have a three-interception performance just two weeks ago. If the Steelers' defense can force a turnover or two and give their offense support with shorter fields, that will go a long way in helping them keep pace. On offense, the Steelers continue to long for better production from their pass-catchers to help unlock more downfield plays. Warren has been the team's only consistent playmaker and Rico Dowdle has ran well over the last two weeks in a complimentary role. However, D.K. Metcalf and company have been up-and-down in the passing game. In order to match Cincinnati's high-flying offensive attack, the Steelers will likely need to hit on a few explosive passing plays. Matchup: vs. Houston Texans, 1:00pm EST The Browns have now lost back-to-back games and are looking to get back on track before their upcoming bye week. In Week 9, they allowed a winnable game to slip through their grasp against the Saints, where they lost by one point in overtime. Shedeur Sanders impressed in his spot-start for Deshaun Watson at quarterback, but the Browns still struggled to run the ball and didn't start scoring much until the fourth quarter. Watson is set to return from injury to start this week versus his former team. The Texans have underwhelmed defensively this year but still have one of the league's more talented defenses, which will pose a challenge for the Browns — whose offense has struggled mightily at times this season. Houston has been vulnerable in pass coverage, allowing over 235 passing yards per game, leaving some hope that Watson can hit a downfield shot or two. The Browns will need to connect on some type of explosive plays or find a way to run the ball more effectively. Defensively, the Browns will need to bring their A game, as the Texans have prolific offensively at times in recent weeks. Last Sunday, they scored 44 points and C.J. Stroud threw five touchdown passes with nearly 400 passing yards. The Browns may be able to afford to sell out against the pass rather than the run, as the Texans rank even worse running the ball than they do. Matchup: vs. Los Angeles Chargers, 8:15pm EST The Ravens were thrashed by the Jacksonville Jaguars last Thursday night, losing by 20+ points for the third straight game. Baltimore's offense struggles hit a new low, as the team scored 10 points, gained 10 first downs and totaled just over 200 yards. With a hobbled third-string quarterback under center, the Ravens were no match for a talented Jaguars' squad. Fortunately, they will get the ultimate potential get-right matchup this coming Monday, taking on a winless Chargers team that is in disarray. Hopes for a potential offensive turnaround lie with new incoming quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who the Ravens traded for after Week 9. Brissett should provide a significant upgrade over Joe Fagnano as an experienced veteran who has proven, at the bare minimum, he can lead scoring drives and operate an offense at a competent level. Even with Brissett now under center, the Ravens need more consistency from their offensive line and breakthrough performances from veterans like Mark Andrews, Ronnie Stanley and Derrick Henry. Defensively, the Ravens have given up 30+ points in three straight weeks to three of the best offenses and quarterbacks in the NFL. They've played good halves and quarters, but the lows have been low. Coverage breakdowns and lack of impact pass rush continue to plague them. If there were ever a spot to have a convincing performance and force turnovers, this would be it. Chargers' quarterback Justin Herbert leads all quarterbacks in interceptions this season.

There's probably just a small difference between this division and their NFC equivalents. The Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals are at the top of the division with 6-2 record, while the Browns are in third place with a 5-4 mark. The injury-plagued Baltimore Ravens are in fourth with a 4-5 record. The NFC North has three teams with six victories, while the first-place Chicago Bears have seven. The Steelers and Bengals are meeting Sunday night to determine the leader in the division. The Steelers have taken advantage of another memorable season from quarterback Aaron Rodgers . The 42-year-old announced that he would be retiring at the end of the season, and he has come through for head coach Mike McCarthy. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rodgers has completed 175 of 288 passes for 1,871 yards with 13 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. He has always been known for his remarkable accuracy, and while he may no longer be at his peak, he is completing 60.8 percent of his passes. The years have slowed him down a bit when it comes to running out of the pocket, and that's something that Rodgers wants to avoid. The Bengals are surging as they prepare for this game against their division rivals. They have won four straight games after a 2-2 start and they are anxious to establish their explosive offense against the nasty Steelers defense. The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 when the two teams met in Pittsburgh in Week 3. Dynamic QB Joe Burrow will throw for 250-plus yards and 3 TDs Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images There's little doubt that Joe Burrow is among the most gifted quarterback in recent memory. Burrow has been troubled by injuries in recent years, but he is healthy and has been showing off his remarkable skill level through the first half of the season. Burrow has completed a shocking 74.0 percent of his passes. He has connected on 219 of 296 passes for 2,386 yards with 23 TDs and 6 interceptions. He appears to be in the lead when it comes to the race for this season's Most Valuable Player award. Burrow has a remarkable 1-2 punch at the wide receiver position with Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase dominating opposing defensive backs. Higgins has caught 48 passes for 758 yards with 6 TDs, and he uses his speed and big-play ability to light up the scoreboard on a regular basis. Chase may be the best receiver in the NFL, although Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks gives him a solid run for the title. Chase has 53 receptions for 647 yards and 7 TDs. Burrow will always look for Chase when the game is on the line. In addition to Higgin and Chase, tight end Mike Gesicki is an excellent red zone weapon, and he could be dangerous in this game. He has caught 26-252-6 through eight games. Rodgers will throw a pair of TD passes to his tight ends The Steelers don't have the superstars at the wide receiver position that the Bengals possess, but Rodgers has demonstrated that he doesn't need the same kind of big plays that the Bengals regularly produce. Wideout DK Metcalf is leading the Steelers in reception. He has caught 33 of 65 targets for 378 yards with 1 TD. More has been expected from Metcalf, and he needs to play more consistently in the second half of the season. The most productive receivers the Steelers have for red zone activity are tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth. Washington uses his size and strength to catch the ball in the end zone. He has 19 receptions for 254 yards and 3 TDs. Freiermuth has a bit more range than Washington, and he has caught 25-235-4. Running back Jaylen Warren has also demonstrated that he can catch passes out of the backfield in addition to his solid ground attack. Warren has caught 25-294-1, and he is also the team's leading rusher 704 yards, a 5.9 yards per carry average and 2 TDs. T.J. Watt will try to limit Burrow's production with 2.0 sacks If the Steelers are going to hold the Bengals' offensive production in check, it will almost certainly involve a powerful game from outside linebacker T.J. Watt. He leads the Bengals with 7.5 sacks and 9.5 tackles for loss. He also has 3 passes defensed, 1 interception that he returned for a touchdown, 1 forced fumble and 1 fumble recovery. Linebacker Payton Wilson is also a key contributor with a team-leading 69 tackles, 7 tackles for loss, 3 passes defensed, 1 interception and 1 fumble recovery. The Steelers rank 7th in total defense, as they are allowing 305.6 yards per game. They are even better as a scoring defense, ranking 4th and allowing just 18.0 points per game. If the Steelers are going to keep the Bengals in check and prevent Burrow from having a huge game, Watt & Co. will have to come up with a peak effort here. home.blurb: Left guard Dylan Fairchild (pectoral), is the new name to monitor this week. Fairchild injured his pectoral late in last Sunday’s victory over the Atlanta Falcons. It caused him to miss the very last snap of the game. Coach Zac Taylor told reporters Wednesday that they’ll take Fairchild day-to-day. Being limited to start the week off is a positive sign. Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) was also limited. There was a chance he wouldn’t play last Sunday, but he was able to Stay in the field for nearly the entire game. Cincinnati will likely take it easy with him until his ankle is fully healed. Defense end Cedric Johnson is notably not included in the injury report, A great sign that his ankle/foot Injury from last week is no longer a concern. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen had his usual rest day. Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column. Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston. Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore. I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track. Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable. Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards. The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver. In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story. Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do. Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9. There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches. Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance. Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play. This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory. Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? This is one of its best remaining opportunities to avoid that nightmare, and I'm picking the Chargers to take advantage. Los Angeles is 0-8, the NFL's only remaining winless team. Baltimore has dropped four in a row to plummet to the bottom of the AFC North after a 4-1 start. Someone will win in primetime. The 33-year-old gives Baltimore veteran leadership and a chance to make the playoffs after a 4-5 start. home.headline: Report: Lamar Jackson Informed Ravens Teammates Of Intent To Return In 2026
home.blurb: Report: Lamar Jackson Informed Ravens Teammates Of Intent To Return In 2026 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks Report: Lamar Jackson Informed Ravens Teammates Of Intent To Return In 2026 While it doesn't feel like there's much to be hopeful about as it pertains to the Charm City franchise, the face of it isn't ready to throw in the towel just yet. According to a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , star quarterback Lamar Jackson told his teammates that he plans to return this season, with the hope of leading them on a late-season push for the postseason. After starting the season winning four of their first five games, the Ravens now sit at 4-5 and currently sit outside of the current playoff picture at the bottom of the AFC North division standings. With eight games and a bye week remaining on their schedule, in order to return to the postseason after just falling short last year, they'll need to start stacking some wins. The earliest Jackson is eligible to return is Week 14, when the Ravens host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, following the team's Week 13 bye. That will be five weeks post-op and at the earliest possible end of the spectrum for his potential return. If the Ravens can rattle off four straight wins or at least go 2-2 over that span, they'll be in a great position to make Jackson's push to return worthwhile. It'd be just in time for their final four games, all of which are against AFC North rivals, including a pair of bouts with the current division-leading Pittsburgh Steelers. If the Ravens want keep any glimmer of hope of still being alive and in contention for the postseason by the time Jackson is able to return to action, they can't afford to lose to the only winless team in the league. It might end up being a battle of backup quarterbacks if the Chargers decide to sit Herbert so he doesn't embarass himself or get further banged up in primetime. home.headline: Ravens' Lamar Jackson's Reported Injury and Return Timeline Revealed
home.blurb: Ravens' Lamar Jackson's Reported Injury and Return Timeline Revealed - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks Ravens' Lamar Jackson's Reported Injury and Return Timeline Revealed Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was placed on IR after it was revealed that he suffered a significant thumb injury in Week 8. It was not known what had occurred officially or how long he would be out. That information has now reportedly been revealed. NFL insider Ian Rapoport has revealed that Jackson is dealing with a fractured and dislocated thumb, and he will be out for most of the rest of the regular season. The report states that Jackson will be out for six to nine weeks due to the thumb injury. He struck his hand on the helmet of a Buffalo Bills defender on the first play of the game, leading to him being ruled out. If that timeline holds, it would place the quarterback's return on Dec. 13, which is Week 14 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. With Jackson out and backup Tyler Huntley out for the season, the Ravens leapt into action to secure a veteran presence. That veteran is Jacoby Brissett. There is plenty more football left to play, but the Ravens have to start winning some games to keep things alive until Jackson can return. Sources: Mauricio Pochettino leaving USMNT for Manchester United TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Poch's looming Man United move (Mark Konezny-Imagn Images) James Brizuela · Roundtable Sports Sun, November 8, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Rapoport stated that, through league sources, Jackson held a meeting with the Ravens team, and the messaging was basically to "stay alive." The quarterback has every intention of returning this season and could do so if Baltimore makes it into the playoffs. If the timeline goes past those six weeks, Jackson will presumably be back by Week 17, putting him back into action against the Cincinnati Bengals on Dec. 31. This is all just a presumption, as Jackson could need more time to heal from the thumb injury. Projections are simply that: an idea of when a player would heal from the injury. Brissett was sent over to the Ravens from the Arizona Cardinals. Baltimore gave up a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick, while receiving Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick. It seems like a steep price to pay for the Ravens, who now have minimal picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. Brissett is a proven veteran but fell down the depth chart in Arizona due to some early-season struggles. He does have the kind of arm and rush prowess that may fit well with the way Baltimore plays. Brissett will presumably make his debut as the Ravens starter in Week 10, as the team faces the Los Angeles Chargers. Baltimore is currently on a four-game losing streak, and they sit at 4-5. They cannot afford to lose many more games if they want to compete for a playoff spot
